data.description:
The delivery-health screen tells an organizer to "send the decision again". The
system will not do it. This ticket makes that sentence true.

THE DEFECT
notifyExistingDecisions (src/jobs/cascade/decisions.ts:441), behind
POST /api/v1/events/{eventId}/submissions/not-notified/notify, excludes any
submission that already has an outbox row at status='sent':

  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM outbox sent WHERE ... sent.status = 'sent' ...)

Since a send is marked 'sent' the moment the provider accepts it, a speaker
whose acceptance hard-bounced is both invisible to the health screen AND refused
by the retry tool. The one failure this product exists to prevent — a speaker
never learning they were accepted — is fully reachable today.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM MRQ-79
Detection and recovery have different costs and different dependencies. MRQ-79
needs a deployment and a provider dashboard step. This needs neither, and it
covers the case no provider will ever report: the speaker emails you saying they
never got it. Recovery is useful without classification; classification is
nearly useless without recovery.

WHAT IT DOES
- A per-record action: "This did not reach them — fix the address and send
  again." It mints a fresh idempotency key (the retryKey pattern at
  decisions.ts:504 already does this) so a NEW outbox row is created even when
  the prior row is 'sent'.
- An organizer-set "not received" mark on the record, so a message a human knows
  bounced lands on the delivery-health ledger without waiting for any provider
  to tell us. At most one nullable column.
- Health-screen rows that are actionable rather than advisory.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Editing a speaker's email and choosing send again produces a new outbox row
   and a real send — verified end to end, not just at the endpoint.
2. Marking "not received" puts the speaker back on the ledger with the decision
   intact and no duplicate decision written.
3. The daily 100-send cap is respected: recovery sends queue like any other and
   never bypass the outbox.
4. Idempotent under double-click — one action, one message.
5. Demo mode still holds the mail back exactly as configured.

WHEN DONE: there is no stuck case an organizer cannot get out of, whether or not
anything ever told us the message failed.
data.title: Recovery — let an organizer fix an address and actually resend

data.body: One thing already reachable without any webhook: a hard bounce puts the address on Resend's account-level suppression list, so a SECOND send to it fails synchronously with a distinctive message. The classifier landed in 2f0e426 already reads that as address_suppressed and tells the organizer to get a different address. For a one-shot acceptance email that second send only happens if this ticket's recovery action exists — which is the argument for doing this one first.

Board reconciliation 2026-08-12: VERIFIED STILL REAL — stays in backlog. The defect this ticket names is present on github/main today. src/jobs/cascade/decisions.ts still carries the exclusion in notifyExistingDecisions: 'AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM outbox settled ... AND (settled.status = 'sent' OR ...))'. A send is marked 'sent' the moment the provider accepts it, so a speaker whose acceptance hard-bounced is still both invisible to the delivery-health screen and refused by the retry tool. Nothing merged has touched this path. MRQ-74, which carried the bounce-classification and honesty pass, is now closed as done — but it closed the screen's lying, not this recovery gap, which is exactly the separation this ticket's 'WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM MRQ-79' section predicted.

Plan authored 2026-08-12 by agent:board-reconciler at the operator's direction ('make a plan yourself then give it to luna to build'), verified against github/main @ 75b871d9. Plan is at .lattice/plans/. Worktree and branch prepared. Builder: codex gpt-5.6-luna at max effort. Three tickets are being built in parallel and the plan states the file-ownership boundary between them explicitly — MRQ-128 owns outbound webhook_endpoints/webhook_deliveries and /settings/webhooks, MRQ-79 owns the inbound Resend route and migration 0013, MRQ-80 owns decisions.ts and the recovery action.

Claimed MRQ-80 as agent:delegator-mrq-80. Baseline is 75b871d9 on the isolated worktree; npm ci restored dependencies, then npm test reached an existing demo bulk test failure because RESEND_API_KEY is absent in this environment. Scope is deliberately: reuse canonical speaker address PATCH, add a distinct per-record resend that creates a fresh outbox attempt while preserving notifyExistingDecisions sent exclusion, and make the existing delivery-health record link actionable. No migration or MRQ-79 inbound-state work.

Live Worker proof observed on npx vite dev at 127.0.0.1:51980 (build 75b871d94c6f): authenticated record GET returned actions.can_resend_decision=true; canonical PATCH /events/evt-mrq80-live/speakers/person-mrq80-live-speaker changed live-old@example.test to live-new@example.test; POST /submissions/sub-mrq80-live/decision/resend returned 202 with a fresh outbox_id; record history showed to_email=live-new@example.test and unchanged decision id; outbox read showed the new row targeting live-new@example.test with a new 64-character idempotency key and status=suppressed/suppressed_reason=demo_mode_not_allowlisted; bulk POST /submissions/not-notified/notify returned selected=0, queued=0. This proves the real Worker path and demo-safe queue behavior.

Implementation checkpoint: deliberate resend is a new per-record POST path and fresh outbox attempt; the existing bulk SQL still includes settled.status = 'sent'. The existing speaker PATCH path remains the address edit seam, and the record page now offers Edit speaker address plus Send decision again. No migration or MRQ-79 state was added. Focused recovery tests pass 3/3; trace:ac is pass with no errors.

Validation observed against a running Worker at 127.0.0.1:51980 (build 75b871d94c6f): PATCH the canonical speaker address returned 200; the submission record returned can_resend_decision=true and the corrected participant email; POST /api/v1/events/evt-mrq80-live/submissions/sub-mrq80-live/decision/resend returned 202 with a fresh outbox id; record history showed submission.decision_resent and unchanged decision_id; outbox showed the new row at the corrected address with a fresh 64-character idempotency key and demo-safe suppression; POST bulk notify returned selected=0, queued=0 and did not add an outbox row.

MRQ-80 now has a deliberate per-record decision resend using the corrected current speaker address and a fresh outbox identity; the existing bulk-notify settled.status = 'sent' exclusion remains intact.
